chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Mu'adh, from Abu Arakah, who said:

I prayed the Fajr prayer behind Ali (peace be upon him) in this mosque of yours, then he turned towards his right side, and a sorrowful disposition was upon him until the sun rose over the wall of this mosque of yours to the extent of a spear, and it is not there today. Then he turned to the people and said: 'By Allah, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would spend this night in it, alternating between their foreheads and their knees [in prostration and bowing]. When morning came, they rose up dusty and pale, with a mark between their eyes like the knee of a goat. When Allah was mentioned, they would bend as a tree bends on a windy day, and their eyes flowed [with tears] until their clothes became wet.' He said: Then he stood up while saying: 'By Allah, it is as though the people spent the night in negligence.' Then he was not seen laughing until the wicked one did what he did.'

key_terms.الْفَاسِقِ: the wicked one (referring to Ibn Muljam)
key_terms.شَبَهُ رُكْبِ الْمَعْزَى: like the knee of a goat (a mark of prostration)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali observe about the worship habits of the Prophet's companions?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) profound spiritual state, characterized by a visible aura of solemnity (*ka'aba*) and deep contemplation during Fajr prayer. Abu Arakah contrasts the intense, physical devotion of the Prophet’s companions—marked by alternating prostration and bowing—with the spiritual negligence that eventually led to the rise of the *Fasiq* (transgressors), underscoring the Shia emphasis on the transition from the era of pure devotion to the period of political and spiritual decline.
